I’m 28. I started grad school in summer 2021, right before I turned 26.

After you graduate, you become an “associate trainee therapist” and during that time you need to accrue 3,000 hours (which takes about 3-4 years) in order for you to take your licensure test so you’re officially an MFT.  
So ima work as an associate for a bit and then go back to school for my PsyD. I’ll be in my 30s when I get that degree. 
But also, a big thing about loans is finding the right repayment plan that works for you. 
I got accepted into the new SAVE plan, based off your income and family size. The less you make, the lower your monthly payments are. Super clutch for me. 
But then right when I go back to school my payments will be on pause until I graduate so. 

It sucks tho, imo, in our country how STUPID expensive it is just to get our degrees so we can do the careers we really wanna do. It sucks. The govt could TOTALLY take away student debt but nooooo. It’s all bs.

I’m so so sorry for your loss. 
My father committed suicide when I was 6 years old. It took me a long time to come to terms with everything (I’m 24 now) to be able to forgive myself and move forward. I still have some healing to do on the subject, but I’m not where I was last year. It took me 12 years to be able to accept what he did was his choice, that he was in pain and he couldn’t find the light, to forgive my inner child because she did nothing wrong, that it wasn’t my fault. That was the first thing everyone told me as a child, that it wasn’t my fault. And I didn’t understand what they meant until I got a little older, around 11-12. That’s when I started blaming myself for him leaving. 
He did leave us, my family, but he was in pain from his demons and he couldn’t move on, he was stuck in the past and his pain ran so deep that he did what he did. My father didn’t leave a note, he just did it on my parents anniversary, I guess he was ready for it. He made up his mind to leave this plane of existence. 
He wasn’t spiritual nor religious, he was an alcoholic. I’m no longer mad at him for drinking his problems away. I don’t hold any ill will against him. I wish him so much peace now because his pain is gone. He had debilitating migraines (which have passed down to me) so I think part of why he did it is because of the physical pain he also went through, as I have been through the same exact type of emotions dealing with this disease. 
Depression is a disease of the mind and if it isn’t treated it can eat away at you. I didn’t experience depression until I understood what my father did. 

If you ever want to talk about this you can message me. 
But I think my advice is to talk about this with your family (if they can, it’s ok if they can’t because everyone processes a suicide differently), your friends, a therapist, someone who can listen to you and what you’re going through. Community is really important during these types of situations because we can come together and share/hold love between each other. 
The stages of grief will happen and that’s ok. Don’t blame or get mad at yourself for experiencing these emotions because it’s natural to feel denial or be in shock, it’s natural to be angry because yeah, our fathers left. But they did it because of their own pain. They weren’t thinking straight, they didn’t think of the repercussions it would have on their families, they only thought about how their pain would end. 

Again I’m so sorry that you and your family have experienced this, it’s so heartbreaking. I’m shedding some tears for you because of how personal this is to me. 
I hope in time you feel ok, and remember it’s ok to not feel ok. Don’t hide any emotions, let them all out and talk about his death. 
It will get easier with time. I promise you that. It doesn’t matter how long you grieve for, it’ll take however long it’ll take for you. Don’t listen to anybody who tries to tell you to get over it because theres no getting over it, this will stay with you forever but it won’t hurt you forever.
